name: OpenAPI
tagline: Give Stuntman the provider's OpenAPI or Swagger spec and it answers like the API: routes, answers, schema checks and the token route.
stands_in_for: JSON or YAML specs with $ref files
point: the spec's server host on :8443, Test CA trusted

capabilities.title: A route per operation
capabilities.text: Each path and method becomes a route with the server's base path in front; the operationId is kept.

capabilities.title: Answers from the spec
capabilities.text: The lowest 2xx is the default; every other response becomes a named answer like payment_required or not_found.

capabilities.title: Built when no example
capabilities.text: From the schema: ids that change per call, now() for date-time, and fields that echo what the app sent.

capabilities.title: Bodies checked
capabilities.text: Types, required, enums, allOf, oneOf, additionalProperties: false and date, date-time, email formats; a bad body gets the spec's 400 or 422.

capabilities.title: Token route included
capabilities.text: OAuth2 client credentials in the spec add a token route at its tokenUrl; routes using it require a Bearer token.

capabilities.title: Webhooks ready to send
capabilities.text: 3.1 webhooks and 3.0 callbacks become webhook_<name> answers holding their payloads.

capabilities.title: The spec served back
capabilities.text: Kept with the files its $refs point to, so clients generated from it work unchanged.

capabilities.title: Re-import keeps edits
capabilities.text: A new version adds routes; your steps, answers, data and settings stay. Routes it lacks are listed in notInSpec.

excerpts.title: A new service from a spec

callouts.title: Start from a spec
callouts.text: OpenAPI 3.x, Swagger 2.0 or a WSDL; Stuntman tells which one it is.

callouts.title: URL or file
callouts.text: Files the spec points to with $ref are read too.

callouts.title: Check bodies
callouts.text: A body that breaks the schema gets the provider's 400 error.

callouts.title: What the spec has
callouts.text: Every route with the responses it declares, before anything is created.

callouts.title: OAuth from securitySchemes
callouts.text: Client credentials on /oauth/token, any client accepted until you add some.

excerpts.title: Routes made from the spec are normal routes

callouts.title: Routes from the spec
callouts.text: One per operation, with calls today.

callouts.title: Receive
callouts.text: Bearer token from /oauth/token; the body is checked against ChargeRequest, else the invalid answer.

callouts.title: Decide
callouts.text: Rules you add pick the spec's other responses: a card ending 0002 gets 402.

callouts.title: Re-import the spec
callouts.text: Reads a new version and keeps your steps; the served spec is one click away.

callouts.title: Path it lacks
callouts.text: A call to a path the spec does not have shows in Unmatched.

callouts.title: One per response
callouts.text: Marked example (the spec's example) or schema (built from the schema).

callouts.title: Reset to the spec
callouts.text: Edit an answer to match the real provider, or go back to what the spec said.

callouts.title: Checked against the schema
callouts.text: The body is a template checked against the response schema.

callouts.title: Timeline sentence
callouts.text: What the call leaves on the timeline, as a template.

callouts.title: What the app gets
callouts.text: Status, headers and body, filled from the last call.

provoke.name: Any declared response
provoke.what: 402, 404, 409 or any response the spec declares, on the next calls

provoke.name: Validation error
provoke.what: A body that breaks the schema gets the spec's 400 or 422 naming the field

provoke.name: Expired token
provoke.what: Every token becomes invalid; the next call gets 401

provoke.name: Missing token
provoke.what: A route that uses the OAuth scheme refuses a call without Bearer

provoke.name: Undeclared response
provoke.what: An answer the spec does not have

provoke.name: Network and server failures
provoke.what: Reset, empty, timeout, 500, 503 or an HTML page

provoke.name: Slow or flaky
provoke.what: Latency on every answer, or a random share of failures

provoke.name: Path not in the spec
provoke.what: The app calls a version the spec lacks; it answers 404 no route

advantages.title: Right on the first call
advantages.text: A 201 that echoes the amount and currency the app sent, without writing a line.

advantages.title: Every response reachable
advantages.text: Responses a sandbox rarely returns come on cue: 402, 409, 422, 503.

advantages.title: Contract drift caught
advantages.text: Bodies that break the schema are refused, and calls to paths the spec lacks are listed.

advantages.title: Follows new versions
advantages.text: Re-import the provider's new spec without losing the rules you added.

agent.prompt: Stand in for the payments API from its OpenAPI spec and test a declined card at checkout.
tools: A service from OpenAPI 3.x, Swagger 2.0 or a WSDL
Reads the spec again and keeps your steps
Named answers and which route uses each
Creates or replaces a named answer
Runs a route on a sample request
The next calls get a named answer
Calls to paths no route takes

notes: Only JSON bodies are checked; pattern, lengths, numeric ranges and discriminator are not. Path, query and headers are not checked.
API keys and OAuth flows other than client credentials are not checked.
